chapters.3.meaning: Ruth asks Boaz to act as a family protector. He promises to settle the matter with the closer relative.
chapters.4.summary: Boaz meets the nearer relative and witnesses at the town gate. He marries Ruth. Their son Obed becomes David’s grandfather.
chapters.4.meaning: The witnesses confirm Boaz’s duty toward Ruth and the family’s land. Naomi’s household gains a future.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me compares Boaz’s care with Jesus Christ’s power to redeem.
people.orpah.meaning: Orpah weeps when leaving Naomi. She returns home with Naomi’s blessing.
people.nearer-redeemer.relations: A closer relative of Elimelech than Boaz.
people.nearer-redeemer.meaning: He offers to buy the land but withdraws when the duty also includes Ruth.
people.jesse.meaning: The closing family list connects Jesse with Obed and David.
people.david.role: Later king descended from Ruth and Boaz
people.perez.meaning: The witnesses ask that Ruth’s household grow like Perez’s family.
people.hezron.role: Son of Perez and ancestor of Boaz
people.hezron.meaning: Hezron’s name connects Perez with Ram in the closing family list.
people.ram.role: Son of Hezron and ancestor of Boaz
people.ram.meaning: Ram appears between Hezron and Amminadab in the family list.
people.amminadab.role: Father of Nahshon and ancestor of Boaz
people.amminadab.relations: Son of Ram. Father of Nahshon.
people.nahshon.role: Father of Salmon and ancestor of Boaz
people.nahshon.meaning: Nahshon’s son Salmon becomes the father of Boaz.
people.leah.meaning: The witnesses recall Leah when blessing Ruth. They honor her part in building Israel’s family.
people.rachel.meaning: The witnesses recall Rachel alongside Leah when blessing Ruth’s future household.
people.judah.meaning: The witnesses remember Judah’s family through Tamar and Perez.
people.tamar.meaning: The witnesses recall Tamar as Perez’s mother. Her family gives them a pattern for blessing Ruth.
